chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning one who killed, drank wine, and stole: he carried out the hadd upon him, so he flogged him for drinking wine, cut off his hand for his theft, and killed him for his killing.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.قَتَلَهُ: he executed him for the act of killing
key_terms.قَطَعَ يَدَهُ: he amputated his hand as the punishment for theft

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام for someone who killed, drank wine, and stole?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding a person who combined multiple crimes: killing, drinking wine, and theft. The ruling applies the prescribed punishment for each offense, showing the administration of judicial penalties in accordance with each individual crime.
